world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Dieu, Michel & Louis Perrois 2016. Dictionnaire encyclopedique koma gimbe / francais (Monts Alantika, Nord-Cameroun)

new_statements.quote: Beiya and its Nigerian variant Gindoo is spoken in the southern part of the Alantika Mountains and the adjacent foothills and plains in Cameroon (Northern Region) and Nigeria (Adamawa State) from Wangay (Cameroon) to Tantile (Nigeria) (Kleinewillinghöfer 2015). There are an estimated 39.000 speakers for Beiya. The phoneme inventory of this tonal language consists of 20 consonants and 15 vowels. It has a full functioning noun class system.
new_statements.citation: Littig, Sabine. 2018. What happens to the adjective class in Samba-Duru? The expression of qualification in Kolbila, Duru and Beiya. Arbeitspapiere des Instituts für Ethnologie und Afrikastudien der Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz 180.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Beiya (the main Gəmnəm/Gimnime lect) is described as a tonal language; no statement about word stress or accent is made in any accessible source. Second-hand (Fabre 2020: 135, summarising Dieu's sketch in the 2016 dictionary): 'Sur le plan tonal, les auteurs mentionnent trois tons ponctuels et deux tons modulés' = three level tones and two contour tones; again nothing on stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is a one-sentence typological profile in a morphosyntax working paper by a fieldworker on Beiya; the only dedicated phonological sketch (Dieu in Dieu & Perrois 2016, 3 pp.) was not accessible and could contain an accent remark.
new_statements.identity_note: All accessible first-hand material is on the Beiya lect (with Gindoo and Riitime) of Gəmnəm/Gəmnəme, which Kleinewillinghöfer 2015 and Littig 2020 equate with Gimnime [gmn, gimn1238]; Dieu & Perrois's 'koma gɨ́mbē' is the same language (Boyd 1989: 'the Gɨmbe speaking Gɨmnɨme'; Glottolog files the dictionary under gimn1238). Not to be confused with the sister language Gimme/Kompana/Panme [kmp, gimm1239] or the northern 'Koma' lects (Gəunəm, Vɔmnəm, Damtəm), which are Vere-group.

There are an estimated 39.000 speakers for Beiya. The phoneme inventory of this tonal language consists of 20 consonants and 15 vowels. It has a full functioning noun class system.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. One-line typological profile of Beiya (Gəmnəm = Gimnime), p.1: 'The phoneme inventory of this tonal language consists of 20 consonants and 15 vowels.' Data are tone-marked (e.g. low vs high tone on verbal-noun suffix -gə̀l / -gə́l).

sources.citation: Fabre, Gwenaëlle. 2020. Review of Michel Dieu, Louis Perrois & Henry Tourneux, Dictionnaire encyclopédique koma-gɨ́mbē/français (monts Alantika, Nord-Cameroun). Linguistique et Langues Africaines 6: 133-136. doi:10.4000/lla.312
sources.note: Second-hand summary of the dictionary's 3-page phonological sketch (pp.134-135): 9 short + 9 long oral vowels, 3 short/5 long nasal vowels, 21 consonants, vowel-length contrast neutralised in closed syllables; 'Sur le plan tonal, les auteurs mentionnent trois tons ponctuels et deux tons modulés.' No mention of stress/accent.
